headline: Standardizing heterogeneous biomedical data into queryable knowledge bases and atlases
label: Curated Biomedical Knowledge Databases
summary: Recent preprints and a publication describe curated resources linking biomarker, drug-response, toxicity, and disease evidence for cross-study reuse.
synthesis: The shared thread is curation and harmonization of heterogeneous biomedical evidence into reusable, queryable resources. BiomarkerKB harmonizes biomarker data under a BEST-based model and exposes a Neo4j graph of over 200,000 associations integrated into the CFDE. PharmGEO standardizes 7,931 drug-response transcriptomic experiments across 1,334 drugs, reprocessed through a single pipeline and served as a Shiny atlas. IBDkb integrates literature, trials, drugs, targets and compounds for inflammatory bowel disease, with AI-assisted search. The cross-species study computes preclinical-to-human toxicity concordance for 7,565 drugs via likelihood ratios, with an open web app. The novelty lies in standardized cross-study integration rather than in the underlying data types, which differ across the set.
